questions.prompt: Prove that √2 is irrational.

source.reference: Original ExamGuru question authored for CBSE Class X Mathematics 2026–27 summative assessment.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Assume √2 = p/q, where p and q are coprime positive integers. Squaring gives p² = 2q², so p is even; write p = 2k. Then q² = 2k², so q is also even. This contradicts that p and q are coprime. Hence √2 is irrational.

markingScheme.criterion: Assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms and obtain p² = 2q² (1 mark).
Deduce that p and q are both even (1 mark).
State the contradiction and conclusion (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Prove that √3 is irrational.

source.reference: Original ExamGuru question authored for CBSE Class X Mathematics 2026–27 summative assessment.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Assume √3 = p/q in lowest terms. Then p² = 3q², so 3 divides p. Put p = 3k; substitution gives q² = 3k², so 3 divides q as well. This contradicts gcd(p,q) = 1. Therefore √3 is irrational.

markingScheme.criterion: Assume a lowest-terms fraction and obtain p² = 3q² (1 mark).
Show that 3 divides both p and q (1 mark).
Contradiction with coprimality; conclude irrationality (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Using the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, explain why 6ⁿ cannot end in the digit 0 for any positive integer n.

source.reference: Original ExamGuru question authored for CBSE Class X Mathematics 2026–27 summative assessment.

answerKey.modelAnswer: A number ending in 0 is divisible by 10 = 2 × 5, so its prime factorisation must contain a factor 5. But 6ⁿ = 2ⁿ × 3ⁿ contains only the primes 2 and 3. By uniqueness of prime factorisation, it cannot be divisible by 5 and cannot end in 0.

markingScheme.criterion: A number ending in 0 must contain prime factor 5 (1 mark).
Use uniqueness of prime factorisation to conclude (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Tangent geometry: A circular fountain has centre O and radius 5 m. From external point P, tangent PA touches it at A. The distance OP is 13 m.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Mathematics 2026–27 question; eligible for the specified examination slot.

questions.stimulus: A circular fountain has centre O and radius 5 m. From external point P, tangent PA touches it at A. The distance OP is 13 m.

parts.prompt: What is the angle between radius OA and tangent PA?
Calculate the length of PA.
A second tangent PB is drawn from P. State PB and justify the relationship.
parts.answerKey: PB=PA=12 m, because tangents from the same external point are equal.

alternatives.prompt: Tangents QA and QB from another external point Q are equal. If QA=15 cm, find QB and name the theorem.
alternatives.answerKey: QB=15 cm by the equal-tangents theorem.

answerKey.modelAnswer:
(a) 90°.
(b) PA=√(OP²−OA²)=√(13²−5²)=12 m.
(c) PB=PA=12 m, because tangents from the same external point are equal.
